headline: Revenue surges on acquisitions; GAAP swings to a loss
summary_short: Revenue grew 31% year-over-year to $3.0 billion, including $388 million from the CyberArk and Chronosphere acquisitions. GAAP net income swung to a $177 million loss (-$0.22 diluted EPS) from $262 million a year earlier on acquisition-related amortization and stock compensation.
summary_long: Q3 FY26 revenue rose 31% y/y to $3.0B, with product and subscription/support revenue both up 31%, lifted by the CyberArk (closed Feb 2026) and Chronosphere acquisitions. Gross margin compressed to 67.6% from 72.9% on higher intangible amortization and cloud-hosting costs; operating margin fell to -6.1% from 9.6% as opex rose on acquisition-related headcount, severance, and stock compensation. GAAP net income swung to a $177M loss (-$0.22 diluted EPS) from $262M; non-GAAP diluted EPS rose to $0.85 from $0.80. NGS ARR grew 60% to $8.1B and RPO grew 36% to $18.4B. Cash and investments totaled $7.0B. Q4 FY26 guidance: revenue $3.345-3.355B, non-GAAP EPS $0.96-$0.98.

drivers.explanation: Growth was driven by increased demand for subscription and support offerings plus contributions from the CyberArk and Chronosphere acquisitions; product revenue also rose on higher software-license and hardware demand.
Compression was primarily due to higher amortization of intangible assets from recent acquisitions, partly offset in product margin by a mix shift toward software licenses.
Opex grew faster than revenue as R&D, sales and G&A personnel costs rose from acquisition-related headcount, accelerated equity-award vesting, and CyberArk integration and severance charges.
The net loss follows the operating loss, partly offset by other income and a smaller tax provision than the prior-year quarter.
Diluted EPS mirrors the net loss, spread over a much larger share count after the 112 million shares issued for the CyberArk acquisition.
Growth includes $1.6 billion of NGS ARR contributed by the CyberArk and Chronosphere acquisitions, on top of organic subscription and support growth.
RPO growth includes $1.8 billion contributed by the CyberArk and Chronosphere acquisitions.
Non-GAAP EPS rose despite the GAAP loss because it excludes the share-based compensation, acquisition and amortization charges that drove the GAAP decline.
Management cited accelerating bookings tied to AI-driven security demand and said the company is ahead of its M&A integration plans, keeping it on track for its FY28 free-cash-flow-margin target.
